# Science Trivia

Science Trivia is a public English-language website for quick science quiz play and science topic discovery. The site is available at https://science-trivia.com. It lets visitors generate a short set of five science trivia questions, answer them, and review the correct answers with clear explanations.

The site is designed for curious readers who want science trivia questions and answers that explain the mechanism behind the fact. It focuses on science topics such as everyday science, the human body, sleep, plants, physics, chemistry, light, color, materials, scale, perception, and neuroscience.

## Main Content
- [Homepage](https://science-trivia.com/): Main entry point for generating a five-question science trivia quiz with answers and explanations.
- [Archive](https://science-trivia.com/archive): Index of biweekly science trivia features.
- Topic archive pages: Published science features are available at URLs in the form `https://science-trivia.com/archive/<topic-slug>`.

## Topic Coverage
- Science Trivia covers science questions and explanations across everyday science, biology, chemistry, physics, astronomy, sleep science, plant science, materials science, human body trivia, perception, neuroscience, light, color, and scientific scale.
- The site is focused on science trivia rather than general trivia across unrelated subjects.

## Discovery Endpoints
- [Sitemap](https://science-trivia.com/sitemap.xml): Canonical URL discovery for crawlable pages.
- [Robots](https://science-trivia.com/robots.txt): Crawl policy reference.

## URL Patterns
- `https://science-trivia.com/`: Interactive science trivia quiz homepage.
- `https://science-trivia.com/archive`: Archive index for published science trivia features.
- `https://science-trivia.com/archive/<topic-slug>`: One science trivia feature article.
- `https://science-trivia.com/legal/privacy`: Privacy policy.
- `https://science-trivia.com/legal/terms`: Terms of service.

## Crawl Notes
- Start from the homepage for the interactive science quiz experience.
- Start from the sitemap for broad canonical URL discovery.
- Use archive topic pages for longer science trivia explanations and themed science facts.
- Prefer canonical HTML pages for user-facing summaries and citations.
